page: Amazon Web Services c5.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor running at a dedicated clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz. This configuration provides 2.0 GB of memory per core. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX and AVX512F instructions.

Performance benchmarks place the c5.2xlarge in the average range for most compute and memory operations. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1175.0 and a multi-core score of 4531.0. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only performance of 437.77 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 50.41 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write speed of 38.06 GB/sec. The server demonstrates solid throughput for static web serving at 7.26 GB/sec and handles Redis SET operations at 7.77 million operations per second. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and LLM inference tasks represent performance bottlenecks, with the 7B model prompt processing dropping to a poor rating of 11.09 tokens per second.

This instance does not include local NVMe storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Network connectivity is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c5.2xlarge offers a dedicated compute-to-RAM ratio of 1:2, making it a resource-dense option for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. It is suitable for batch processing, web serving, distributed analytics, and moderate CPU-based serialization or compilation tasks, but is less optimal for large-scale language model inference or memory-intensive database deployments.
description: Amazon Web Services c5.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor running at 3.4 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor, it delivers dedicated compute resources with an x86_64 architecture. The server lacks local storage and complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data indicates average performance across standard compute, memory, and web serving tasks, though it exhibits limitations in multi-threaded decompression and large language model inference. With a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, this instance provides a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads such as batch processing, web serving, and software compilation that do not require high-capacity local storage or massive memory allocations.
